consumers.evidence: The confirmed product behavior uses an in-task overlay for referenced local files, preserves download, and keeps unsupported document formats truthful.
THREAD-FILE-PREVIEW-001 records mobile and desktop presentation, supported formats, failure behavior, authentication, reference validation, allowed roots, and deferred office conversion.

Current source renders plain Markdown links and has no file-serving route, so implementation can add the feature without preserving a competing preview owner. Existing attachment cleanup remains authoritative.
The contract identifies message hydration, token registration, authenticated HTTP delivery, Markdown rendering, modal state, responsive layout, and regression tests as the affected consumers.
The executable chain is thread open to referenced-path validation to opaque preview token to authenticated file response to in-task overlay and download.
Existing thread hydration, trusted-device sessions, Express delivery, ReactMarkdown, and responsive conversation UI provide the required extension points.
The feature can use Node filesystem and crypto APIs plus current React and Express dependencies; no new runtime or document-conversion dependency is required.
An in-memory server registry owns opaque grants; session authentication and canonical allowed-root validation gate every response; restart and expiry fail closed.
Thread cwd and the existing upload root are the only allowed roots; no new user configuration, permanent index, or generated asset is introduced.

Acceptance covers authentication, referenced-path and canonical-root checks, missing and expired files, active-content blocking, supported previews, download, responsive behavior, scroll preservation, and regressions.
Implementation is authorized now; office conversion, editing, collaboration, permanent file storage, release, and public exposure remain deferred.
Ordinary reversible implementation runs on codex/task-file-preview in the current checkout without Task Control, force push, PR, release, or external publication.
